/bin/bash -lc "python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
p = Path('src/data/lyrics/yun-tere-naam-se-naat.md')
_, header, body = p.read_text().split('---\\n', 2)
roman = header.split('romanLyrics: |-\\n', 1)[1]
for content, numbers in ((roman, '1234567'), (body, '۱۲۳۴۵۶۷')):
    groups = content.strip().split('\\n\\n')
    assert len(groups) == len(numbers)
    for group, number in zip(groups, numbers):
        lines = group.splitlines()
        assert len(lines) == 3 and lines[0].strip() == number
assert 'direction: \"rtl\"' in header and 'noUrdu' not in header
assert '\\u200c' not in body
print('Verified seven matching couplets, 14 verse lines per edition.')
PY"

Reconstructed the Urdu-script body in [yun-tere-naam-se-naat.md](src/data/lyrics/yun-tere-naam-se-naat.md) and preserved the Roman wording in `romanLyrics` with sentence casing. I grouped the 14 lines into seven couplets and verified that the two editions match in stanza and verse counts.
